correctness.rationale: Direct inversion, or the symmetric and antisymmetric eigenvectors of the two-site Gram matrix, gives the exact sinh cardinal functions. On compact t-sets the scaled coefficients h c_± tend to ±t e^(−t²)/2 (assigning the positive sign to c_+); the scaled objective's uniform tail follows from |sinh z|≤|z|e^|z| and the Gaussian factor. Hence every small-h maximizing point lies close to one of ±1/√2, away from the nonsmooth zeros at the sites. In the positive neighborhood, the two absolute scaled coefficients are e^(−t²)/2 times t±h+(t+2t³/3)h²+O(h³). The sum of their p-th powers is even analytic in h there after scaling. Binomial expansion and the 1/p root yield relative correction G(t)=1+2t²/3+(p−1)/(2t²), with C² remainder O_p(h⁴). The second derivative of log(t e^(−t²)) at t_0=1/√2 is −4; strict local concavity and localization give one positive maximizer, reflected to the only negative one. The displacement is G'(t_0)h²/4=√2(2/3−p/2)h². Evaluating at t_0 is accurate through h² by stationarity, and G(t_0)=p+1/3; taking the p-th power gives the claimed relative correction p(p+1/3) and normalization 2^(1−p)/(2e)^(p/2). The interpretation of the powered factor agrees with the cited representer theorem.
residual_risks: Finite grids do not establish localization or uniqueness; the analytic argument does. No uniformity in p at the endpoints or classification at larger separations.

value.rationale: Two nearly coincident sample sites give a minimal natural test of how smooth Gaussian interpolation amplifies coefficient penalties. The theorem identifies the needed growth rate, its exact p-dependent correction and the two worst evaluation points, which remain a positive distance away while the sites collide. An ill-conditioning estimate only would not give the sharp penalty factor or identify those points, and the Laplace comparison shows that even the order of growth is kernel dependent.
residual_risks: Claim concerns a fixed exponent and two sites, not multi-site collisions or general Gaussian interpolation conditioning.
